issue_context.title: Weight of score plugin was reset by extension points because of same name in scheduler framework
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


#### What happened:
Hi, there. We had a customized plugin to extend score/postBind points in scheduler framework. That means it works at score point to priority and record shared data at postBind point. When I used below config. The weight of score plugin didn't work as 6(reset as 1) because of postBind config. Though I can add `weight` to postBind plugin as a workround. But it's a bit confused that **weight** only works on score plugins.

```
plugins:
  score:
    enabled:
    - name: MyPlugin
      weight: 6     ## This value was reset as 1 because of postBind.
  postBind:
    enabled:
    - name: MyPlugin
```

The weight of above would be assigned in order of [PreFilter, Filter, ...Score, PreBind, Bind, PostBind, ...]: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/bc13a38367cef56f77df8f98736a2615527af45f/pkg/scheduler/framework/runtime/framework.go#L122-L132. After that, the score weight would be reset by same name plugins(postBind) after it. This caused `pluginsNeeded()` overrided original score weight in above order: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/bc13a38367cef56f77df8f98736a2615527af45f/pkg/scheduler/framework/runtime/framework.go#L1157-L1164. 

Only score weight assignment is meaningful. Other weights of extension points **shouldn't** have any effect in scheduling procedure. So score weight should affect at last.

#### What you expected to happen:

Above config works for score weighting.

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):

1. You can add one case in unit-test to quick reproduce: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/bc13a38367cef56f77df8f98736a2615527af45f/pkg/scheduler/framework/runtime/framework_test.go
- New plugin satisfied framework.ScorePlugin and framework.PostBindPlugin like:
```
type TestPlugin struct {
	name string
	inj  injectedResult
}

func (pl *TestPlugin) Name() string {
	return pl.name
}

func (pl *TestPlugin) Score(ctx context.Context, state *framework.CycleState, p *v1.Pod, nodeName string) (int64, *framework.Status) {
	return setScoreRes(pl.inj)
}

func (pl *TestPlugin) PostBind(ctx context.Context, state *framework.CycleState, p *v1.Pod, nodeName string) {
}

func (pl *TestPlugin) ScoreExtensions() framework.ScoreExtensions {
	return nil
}
```
- Add new case at `TestListPlugins`: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/bc13a38367cef56f77df8f98736a2615527af45f/pkg/scheduler/framework/runtime/framework_test.go#L2334
```
		{
			name: "Reset score weight",
			plugins: &config.Plugins{
				Score: config.PluginSet{Enabled: []config.Plugin{{Name: testPlugin, Weight: 6}},
				PostBind: config.PluginSet{Enabled: []config.Plugin{{Name: testPlugin}}},
			},
			pluginSetCount: 2,
		},
```
- Verify result of `f.ListPlugins()`. The weight of score plugin was reset as `1`.

#### Anything else we need to know?:

#### Environment:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`):
I met this in v1.17.6
And I verified it's same at master branch. 

- Cloud provider or hardware configuration:
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`):
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`):
- Install tools:
- Network plugin and version (if this is a network-related bug):
- Others:
If it's ok(accepted as an issue), may i pick up this issue?
